I144.note: Research note (2026): the 1912 Van Wyck genealogy and Flatbush records make him the son of Berndt Danielse van Wyck and Anneken Cornelisse van den Engh of Wijk bij Duurstede, arriving in New Netherland about 1660. The descent from the noble Van Asch van Wijck family shown above him in this tree is a 19th-century tradition that researchers have rejected; those links are kept only so the earlier file is not lost.

I210.note: Research note (2026): one of the Hempstead Smiths ("Rock", "Nan" or "Blue" John Smith); his wife is recorded as a Gildersleeve in compiled genealogies, not Elizabeth Wood. See her entry.

I211.note: Research note (2026): no source supports an Elizabeth Wood as wife of John Smith of Hempstead. Compiled genealogies make Jeremiah Smith's mother a Gildersleeve (daughter of Richard Gildersleeve) and show Jeremiah Wood as the husband of Elizabeth SMITH (m. 1640) — the Wood/Smith marriage is most likely reversed by one generation in this tree.

I219.note: Research note (2026): the link from Jacob Van Asch van Wijck down to Cornelius Barentse Van Wyck is not supported by records — genealogists treat the noble Van Asch van Wijck descent as a myth. Kept for reference only.
